Paragraph:
Translation: There Arjuna could see, within the midst of the armies of both parties, his fathers, grandfathers, teachers, maternal uncles, brothers, sons, grandsons, friends, and also his father-in-law and well-wishers-all present there.

Purport: On the battlefield Arjuna could see all kinds of relatives. He could see persons like Bhurisrava, who were his father's contemporaries, grandfathers Bhisma and Somadatta, teachers like Dronacarya and Krpacarya, maternal uncles like Salya and Sakuni, brothers like Duryodhana, sons like Laksmana, friends like Asvatthama, well-wishers like Krtavarma, etc. He could see also the armies which contained many of his friends.
Characters_Involved: Various Relatives and Teachers (Bhisma, Dronacarya, Krpacarya, Salya, etc.)
Situation/Problem_Faced: Positioned between the two armies, Arjuna takes a comprehensive visual inventory of the opposing force. Instead of seeing anonymous soldiers, he recognizes his most intimate familial, social, and educational ties.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna confronts the stark reality of the war. He fully registers the deeply personal nature of the conflict, identifying the specific people he is expected to kill.
Outcome/Resolution: The abstract concept of 'the enemy' dissolves, replaced by the jarring reality of his own kin, setting the stage for a profound internal crisis.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Bandhava (Deep-rooted familial and social bonds that anchor the soul to the material world)
Maya (The illusion that these temporary bodily relationships are ultimate reality)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This verse marks the activation of Arjuna's material attachments. By seeing his family members arrayed for battle, his consciousness shifts from his righteous duty (dharma) as a warrior to his bodily designations and worldly relationships.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Arjuna experiences a sudden cognitive shift from the abstract to the concrete. He transitions from evaluating a military threat to recognizing loved ones. This shatters his psychological distance from the task, exposing him directly to the imminent trauma of violence against his own support system.
